subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
passage: Two-year-old Abhinav had spent a year abroad, where visitors kept an arm's length. Now, on the veranda of his grandparents' village home, aunts swooped in, pinching cheeks and passing him around. His mouth went tight, his fists pushed at hands, and he shouted "No!" His mother, Aditi, saw his eyes searching for her face. "Give him a minute," she said, lifting him onto her hip. He rested his head on her shoulder, then reached one finger toward an aunt's bangle.

qa.q: Where did the aunts pass Abhinav around?
qa.a: They passed Abhinav around on the veranda of his grandparents' village home.

qa.q: What did Aditi seem to want for Abhinav, and what did Aditi notice?
qa.a: Aditi wanted Abhinav to feel safe and unhurried, and noticed the eyes searching for her face.

qa.q: What choice by Aditi helped Abhinav settle?
qa.a: Lifting Abhinav onto her hip and giving a minute, so that the touch of the bangle came in Abhinav's own time.

qa.q: What might Abhinav have been feeling when passed around?
qa.a: Overwhelmed and cross; the tight mouth, pushing fists and shouted No show it.

grounding: A toddler shows discomfort at being passed between strangers' arms, and a parent reads the cue and responds.

subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
passage: In Lisbon, Great-Aunt Rosa scooped up eighteen-month-old Zanele and kissed both cheeks. Zanele giggled and patted her face. Days later in Helsinki, cousins smiled and waved from an arm's length and did not touch. Zanele frowned, held both arms up, whined, then threw a spoon. Hana, Zanele's mother, watched the little eyes go from face to face, checking each adult's stillness. Hana lifted Zanele for a cuddle, and one cousin waved slowly and offered a toy.

qa.q: Where did the cousins wave from?
qa.a: The cousins waved from an arm's length.

qa.q: What did Hana seem to realise from watching Zanele's eyes go from face to face?
qa.a: That Zanele was reading each adult's comfort, checking for stillness or warmth before deciding how to act.

qa.q: What did Hana do that helped, and what did a cousin add?
qa.a: Hana lifted Zanele for a cuddle, and one cousin waved slowly and offered a toy.

qa.q: How did Zanele react differently in Helsinki than in Lisbon?
qa.a: Zanele giggled with Great-Aunt Rosa but frowned, whined and threw a spoon when kept at arm's length, perhaps missing touch.

grounding: A toddler is held by strangers in one place and kept apart in another and reacts to each; a caregiver notices.

subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
passage: I'm Irfan, and on our trip to see family in Naples I watched my little cousin Charu. At the café, a waitress scooped her up and kissed both cheeks. Charu went stiff and twisted to look at Auntie's face. Auntie smiled and nodded. Charu slowly patted the waitress's hair. In Helsinki last week, nobody touched her at all. She kept holding her arms up to strangers.

qa.q: Where did the waitress scoop Charu up?
qa.a: At the café in Naples.

qa.q: What was Irfan feeling while watching Charu with the waitress?
qa.a: Irfan seems curious and a little amused, noticing how Charu checked Auntie's face before relaxing.

qa.q: How could Auntie help Charu when strangers want to hold her?
qa.a: Auntie can stay close, show a calm smile if it is fine, and gently take Charu back if Charu stays stiff.

qa.q: What might it be like for Charu when a stranger suddenly picks her up?
qa.a: It may feel startling and a bit scary, so she looks to Auntie's face to see whether she is safe.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler abroad who is held by strangers in one place and left alone in another, and who reads an adult's comfort.

subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
passage:
Monday: At Nani's house in Delhi, three aunties took turns to cuddle Harish. He pushed at their chins and cried until his mother, Sarika, held him.
Thursday: In a London café, nobody reached for him. Harish held his arms out to a smiling lady. She only waved.
Saturday: An aunty hugged Sarika. Harish watched Sarika laugh, then leaned in too.

qa.q: Where did the three aunties cuddle Harish?
qa.a: At Nani's house in Delhi.

qa.q: What was Sarika feeling as she noticed Harish change over the week?
qa.a: Sarika was probably amused and relieved, seeing that Harish relaxed once he saw her laugh.

qa.q: What could Sarika do if Harish cries when relatives cuddle him?
qa.a: She could take him back calmly and let him watch from her lap until he feels ready.

qa.q: How might the lady in London have seen Harish holding out his arms?
qa.a: She probably felt touched but unsure, and waved instead because she was not used to holding a stranger's child.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler who is held by relatives in one place and kept apart by strangers in another, and who takes cues from his mother's comfort.

subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
passage: Vijay, two, had flown from Toronto to Hyderabad to meet his grandparents. In the colony, neighbours grabbed his cheeks and lifted him up. Vijay froze and stared at his papa, Abhinav. Abhinav smiled and said, "It's okay, that's Rao uncle." Vijay's fists opened. By evening he was sitting on Rao uncle's knee, pulling his moustache.

qa.q: What did Vijay do when the neighbours lifted him?
qa.a: Vijay froze and stared at his papa, Abhinav.

qa.q: How did Abhinav likely feel when Vijay froze?
qa.a: Abhinav was probably a little anxious for Vijay but calm, smiling so Vijay would feel safe.

qa.q: What helped Vijay settle with Rao uncle?
qa.a: Abhinav's calm smile and simple words showed Vijay the neighbour was safe, so he relaxed at his own pace.

qa.q: How might Rao uncle see Vijay pulling his moustache?
qa.a: He would probably feel delighted and warmly accepted by the little visitor.

grounding: It illustrates a visiting toddler held by neighbours unlike at home, who reads his father's comfort to decide how to react.

subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
passage:
"Zeenat, in Istanbul every aunty in the market kissed Aditi's cheeks, and she giggled," Imran said, pushing the pram through the Oslo airport.
"Here nobody even touches her," Zeenat said. "Look." A woman smiled at Aditi from a polite distance. Aditi, just two, stared, then hid in Zeenat's scarf.
"Is she shy today?"
"No. She's watching me. When I'm relaxed, she's relaxed."
Zeenat smiled at the woman. Aditi peeped out, then waved.

qa.q: Where did every aunty in the market kiss Aditi's cheeks?
qa.a: In Istanbul, every aunty in the market kissed her cheeks.

qa.q: Why did Aditi peep out and wave after hiding?
qa.a: Aditi seemed to feel safe again once Zeenat smiled and relaxed, reading her mother's comfort.

qa.q: What helped Aditi feel at ease with a stranger?
qa.a: Zeenat staying relaxed and smiling at the woman showed Aditi it was safe to come out.

qa.q: How might the woman at the airport see her own behaviour?
qa.a: She was probably being kind in her own way, smiling from a polite distance because that is how warmth is shown where she lives.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler travelling abroad who meets very different touch norms and reads her parent's comfort to decide how to react.
